title: Concerning the Generation of Adam.
text:
⟨p.144⟩
57
57: Concerning the begetting of Adam : 57
Once again a Babylonian catechumen asked the Illu-
minator, saying to him: Speak with me, my Lord, and re-
veal forth to me concerning Adam the first man — at the time
when they molded him, in what manner did they depict him,
or in what manner did they beget him?
{0} indeed his begett-
ing — is it like the begetting which they beget today in human-
kind, or rather is there a difference between his begett-
ing and the one they beget today? Since {1} A-
dam was a strong one in his support, his stat-
ure was great according to his other years, having spent many years ex-
isting in the world; he alone was incomparable to those wh-
om we have likened (to him) in being strong. But all the others who were
begotten in his generation — they themselves were likewise in their years. The
men whom they beget today — their {2}
support has shrunk, their {3} of their other years is diminished — {4}
what is it? And the begetting today of {5}they beget {6}
is altered from those of the first ke{7}
⟨p.145⟩
each in his own place. Behold, the other stars also and zodiac-signs endure
forth in their places. Wherefore now (is) the matter — the lifespan and
the years of these last (ones) have shrunk, become small, even still more than
the ancients who belong to the first generations.
{0} however, the Illuminator himself, in his abundant wisdom,
in his great prudence-of-mind, said to this catechu-
-men who had asked him, namely: 'Their fathers were drawn-out, were diminished.'
Since, therefore, there are five types of the powers and
way-leaders set in the sphere of the zodiac-signs and in the heav-
-ens which are above her: they have names there, being {1}
{2}: among them, the first name is the year, the second
{3} is the month, the third is the day, the
{4} is the hour, the fifth is the moment. The five then
{5} and the five houses exist in the sphere and
the heavens. These places have powers in them, being lords over
them. The lord of the year exists, the lord of the month exists,
the lord of the day exists, the lord of the hour exists,
the lord of the moment exists. One (is) to the share of heaven, of his fel-
-low which is above; (one) to the share that is lord over that which is below,
even unto humanity itself which is begotten and the {6}
(cattle), being begotten among these powers. They themselves indeed, the powers,
have received authority from the beginning of the creation unto the end of the cos-
-mos. In the beginning indeed of the generations, the powers being lord
over the years are the ones reigning. Therefore also the offspring which they
{7} in their generations and their times became (people) of (long) 
years, being many in lifespan, in the generation of Adam and
{8} his son, and that of those who came after him, and
after their cessation — they being king, namely the powers being lord over the
years. The powers themselves being lord over the months reigned. Just as
{9}, since they are smaller than the years, in the same way also
{10} this offspring {11} among them — their lifespan is smaller
{12} in the generation of the powers being lord
⟨p.146⟩
We have spent (our) years.
When the authority of the powers which were
master over the months was completed, the powers of the days received authority and
(came) after them. Thus is the way of the days, that they are smaller than the months.
Thus also is the case of the offspring whom they begot from them: their lifetime
is shorter than the lifetime of those whom they begot in the powers which were master
over the months. In this manner, {0} also, is the offspring whom they begot in their
hours and moments — their lifetime is shorter than that of the
months and that of the days.
The Illuminator says to that catech-
umen, the Babylonian: 'Dost thou see how the e-
nd {1} the world has come near, how greatly the lifetime of {2}
men has come down to nothing, how their days have grown short and their {3}
have diminished? For the life and the light {4}
are in the world were in the first generations more abundantly than to-
day's; for this very reason they have grown small in their support, (and) their life-
time has become small in their hand.'
Once again that catech-
umen, the Baby{5}lonian, says to the Illuminator: 'I beseech'
thee, my Lord! As thou hast made (it) known to us, thou hast persuaded
me concerning the matter of the years — that 'For what cause have the y-
ears of the ancients become long? Or for what cause itself
have the latter ones become short?' Thou didst say to me also that 'They have become short in their
other support.' Thou didst say that 'All these have become small by the dimin-
ishing of the life and the light which they have taken from the world.'
Declare to us also this other thing: how have they begotten
the entire offspring of humanity through one male and one
female, Adam and Eve?' The Illuminator says to that catech-
umen: 'Well indeed dost thou seek after this say-
ing — but recognize it, that thou mayest understand it. For thus is (the case) of the
first generations: that they abound in their light, they
are pure in their support, their other years are great. Thus also is{6}
this of their other offspring — they are exceedingly many beyond the offspring of this t{7}ime.
They were spending a great chronos {8} there in {9}
-laze of their mother; afterwards, {10}
⟨p.147⟩
O what a multitude in one womb! There is a time when they beget
five in one womb. There is a time when they beget seven in {1} wo-
mb. There are some who do not exceed these, there are some
in turn (who are) of more than these. For this reason, indeed, the bearing of their {2} has multipl-
ied with their children. The earth was filled with them; they dwelt at
this end. The bearing of the begetting of the ancient men who have been
begotten in the cosmos is altered, much in comparison to today, whi{3}
their conception and their bearing — its likeness is not the begetting
of the latter ones whom they have begotten today in the womb of the wo{4}an.
For those whom they beget today in the {5} generations are
standing small (and) diminished, and, indeed, one by one those whom they be{6}
are not in one womb, but in two parts, or {7}
or more, while they become another (kind) at a remove in their likeness, being small in
their stature, being feeble in their members, their teachings, and {8}
counsel filled with evil. They are men of wickedness; they are afflicted,
they cease from their standing, being miserable. The other death is bad — 
of darkness.
When that catechumen had {9}
heard these words, he worshipped, he gave glory; he said to the Illuminator:
I give thanks to you, my Lord, for you have persuaded my heart, you have {10}
persuaded me with an exhortation concerning these things about which I asked you.
